properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2021
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 926185
Permit API: 129-26518
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Penn Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2021
Comments: On August 4, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Lamacz #1 well site in Penn Township, Westmoreland County. The inspection was conducted as follow up to a release reported to the Department on 7/19/2021, see inspection #3222750 for previous observations and violations related to the release. At the time of inspection, the impacted material appeared to be excavated and placed under a plastic tarp on the well site. The impacted excavation area appeared to be 30’x60’ and approximately 10’ in depth. The excavation appeared to be following a buried black plastic pipe possibly the gathering pipeline. The excavation of the flow path appeared to be 6" deep, 10’ wide and 500’ in length. The excavation appears to be similar to the impacted location observed on 7/19/2021. The operator has installed temporary ES BMPs and what appear to be oil booms on the excavated flow path. The remediation of spill on the well site has uncovered and damaged what appears to be an encapsulated drill pit or onsite waste disposal location. I observed three sections of the torn black plastic sheeting at different elevation within the excavation. The material contained between the black plastic sheets appeared to be dark gray in color and approximately 2" thick. I recommend that the operator identify the contents of the dark gray material and remediate as needed based on the common constituents/indicators of a release related to brine and cuttings. Violations remain outstanding as they relate to the release on 7/19/2021. Additional violations maybe pending further investigation.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/07/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8273603
Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/01/2023
Comments: On May 1, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the Proffitt 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled, however the well did not appear to be equipped for production. The production line from the well did not appear to be connected to a production unit or other visual production apparatus. The pump jack did not appeared to be operational. The well tag did not appear to match the correct operator information, however the API number appeared to be correct. I observed a significant amount of fluid emanating from the well. I screened the fluid, which appeared to be consisted with fluid produced by a coal bed methane well. The release did not appear to be negatively impacting near by aquatic life, ie tadpoles. Prior to leaving the location, I contacted Apollo Resources Representative Jesse Colangelo to inform him of the release. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to correct the condition creating the release. Mr. Colangelo indicated that they would sent someone out to correct the leak. I requested photos of the repair once the release was corrected. Violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid resulting in a release to the ground. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 887755
Permit API: 083-54017
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-29
Comments: The operator contacted Brian Ayers to report multiple spills at the Collins Pine 22 well site the morning of 6/29/2020. This inspection was performed as a complaint inspection to CID #350759. The operator was intending to perform an injection test on this well for a proposed injection well permit. They had a 500 barrel laydown tank on location that was filled with brine over the course of several days prior to the test. The operator noted on arriving at the site 6/29 that the site was wet, and then was able to see that the tank was actively leaking brine. They were able to contact a vac truck operator who sent trucks to empty the tank. A mini excavator was used to dig a small trench on the north side of the site. In the interim, the operator hooked a hose from the tank to drain into the well in order to reduce the level of the tank. The packer in the well failed, which allowed oil to be displaced and flow out the backside of the packer string and onto the ground. The operator noticed the discharge and immediately shut the well in and ceased flowing water. They had a mini excavator on site and dug another interceptor trench in the access road to cut off oil from flowing further down gradient toward Route 6. 1-2 barrels of oil was estimated to have been released from this well. At the time of this inspection, the operator had determined that 3" of water had drained from the full tank prior to discovery of the leak, which occurred at approximately 10 am. Further leaking occurred during the time between discovery and the emptying of the tank at approximately 2 PM. The total loss of brine is estimated to be between 5 and 10 barrels. Various areas surrounding the tank were tested with a soil EC meter, which read between 15 mS and >20 mS. Oil was all contained within the trench or puddles on the location, with no threat of further contamination. The operator intends to have a rolloff container on site this evening and begin to scrape up the contaminated soil on site, starting with the area contaminated with crude oil. A vac truck will be on site should extra encountered.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/20/2025 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/20/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8238471
Permit API: 081-21995
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/20/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of about 20 gallons of produced fluid. The release occurred while a water truck was removing fluid from the temporary storage tanks onsite.Tobias arrived onsite to screen and remediate the impacted area. A vac truck was used to remove some fluid and surface material. The rest of the remediation involved scraping an area that was approximately 100' long by 63' wide. The excavation averaged 1-2" deep with occasional depths of about 8". There was about 40 tons of material removed and placed into 2 dumpsters for disposal.There were some puddles on the pad surface that were screened for conductivity. Those readings ranged between 0.49 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and 1.07 mS/cm. Soil conductivity immediately off the pad and behind the release ranged between 0.15 - 0.18 mS/cm while a puddle in that area was 0.45 mS/cm (Photos 4 and 5). Continuing downslope, conductivities of puddles in the compost filter sock (CFS) were 0.87 - 1.01 mS/cm. The readings continued to drop as the downslope infiltration berms were screened. The conductivity in front of the berm was 0.37 mS/cm and behind the berm it was 0.1 mS/cm. Moving east along the pad and uphill from the release soil conductivities ranged between 0.70 and 0.83 mS/cm and conductivities of puddles were between 1.03 and 1.09 mS/cm.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted and Immediately Corrected for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). It is recommended that the pad be screened under the secondary containment when it is eventually removed.

The SOBM flowed through the flare line, filled the eco tank and then was released from the top of the flare stack. The onsite vac unit and absorbent pads were utilized to collect standing SOBM." The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS prior to reopening the drain. In the interim, the EI stated that the outlet box will be monitored and drained using a vac truck as needed. The Department requested photographs of the extent of the excavation necessary to remediate the spill, specifically around the perforated drainpipe. The EI stated that the plan was to excavate until they reached "clean" pipe and cut away the impacted portion. The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS if this course of action needs to be modified. The Department also recommended that the flare stack either be moved away from the ditch line or have secondary containment installed. According to the EI, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The Department requests a copy of the waste manifest when it is available. The SDS sheet for the drilling mud and PPC/ERP is on-site. According to the secondary containment inspection record at the site, 4/7/21 is listed as the only inspection/incident to have occurred. The Department requests information on when the secondary containment was installed and when the most recent drilling operations began at the site. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the spill. Pending the operator’s response, more violations may be issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/25/2024 to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren county. 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEAR LAKE PROP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2024
Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 8206015
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Columbus Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/27/2021
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 924724
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 5 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface on Pad B. This inspection was only conducted on Pad B. I met with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release which was along the edge of the well site secondary containment in the travel lane near the company man trailer. The area had already been scraped and backfilled at the time of this inspection. The company man said that the release had occurred from a radiator on a cement truck that was offloading into the upright cement tanks at the time. The truck was straddling the edge of the well site secondary containment so the fluid leaked onto the pad surface. The cement trucks were moved onto the secondary containment as of this inspection. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected. The sump that is in place on the opposite side of the pad surface has had a metal lid placed on it. This sump was installed after fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered by the Department in that area of the pad. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump was approximately 1350 uS/cm. The area around the sump on the pad surface was dry during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding in association with this release.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) completed an administrative inspection on Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 10H well (117-22101) located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 7/27/2022. The inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 7/5/2022 inspection (inspection record # 3394821). A puddle located in front of the produced water temporary storage containers held on the northern edge of the pad surface was field measured at ~12.78mS/cm. The operator was notified of the findings from the 7/5/2022 inspection report via phone on the same day. The operator explained that a water truck would be in route to recover the fluids found. Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "Morgan 073" Marcellus well site.Harry Lammy (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday October 30, 2024 to report an estimated 20 gallon produced liquid release to the south end of the pad surface that day.Murray Kush (Repsol, Company Man) showed me where the produced liquid spill occurred when a vac truck overfilled on the south end of the pad surface near the gray cylindrical tanks. Gas Field Services removed the impacted pad material with guidance from Resource Management and placed it in an open top dumpster within 24 hours of the release. Soil in the remediated area has electrical conductivity of 0.02 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test meter. I did not observe any residual impacts from the spill. Violations for the spill are considered immediately corrected.Repsol expanded the flat pad area at this site February - May 2023. They spudded 4 new conductors on March 27, 2023. Precision Drilling 572 drilled the new wells into the Marcellus Shale in February-April 2024, adding to the existing 4 Marcellus wells at this site. Pro Frac hydraulically fractured the 4 new Marcellus wells here August 29-September 16, 2024. Repsol started flowing back liquid from the 4 new Marcellus wells on October 12, 2024 into the 37 tanks on the south end of the pad. They expect to finish flowback operations in about 1 week. Vegetation, rock, and erosion blanket stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Repsol constructed a new bioretention basin on the south end of the site, and removed the old basin.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface. Moist soil in 3 separate areas on the pad has electrical conductivity of 0.02-0.12 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test.Air temp 63FJLP

Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 903931
Permit API: 003-22234
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/06/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/27/2020 as well as a follow up to a previously reported spill from 8/15/2020 which has been reported as remediated. The operator reported that the spill occurred at approximately 9:30 PM when a check valve washed out. The operator reported approximately 1 barrel of Production Fluid was discharged to the ground. When asked via phone on 12/28/2020, Mr. Hardy reported that the operator would remediate the spill in accordance with Act 2. The following is observed: The Act 9 Sign is present, the ERP, PPC, and associated SDS are in the mailbox adjacent (Photo 1). The operator has removed material between GPUs 2H and 3H (Photo 2) thereby constructing a sump approximately a foot and a half deep and nearly the length of the GPU (Photo 11). Background readings taken in the area were between 70 uS and 300 uS (Photo 12 & 13). Readings taken in the vicinity of standing water in the sump were between 2,000 uS and 13,500 uS. Readings of 2,000 uS were detected between the skids of GPU 3H (Photo 16 & 17). GPU 3H is attached to GPU 16H, on the other side of this structure between another piece of Production Equipment was another smaller "sump" (Photo 6). Background in this area was around 500 uS (Photo 7). Readings taken around this sump were detected at 7,000 uS to 13,000 uS (Photo 5 & 8). GPUs 3H and 16H do not appear to have adequate secondary containment. Per the CO&A entered into on 12/17/2020, these are noted as ICS. The Department requests information on how the operator is going to remediate the impacted material in accordance with 91.33(B) and submit it before 1/11/21. Additionally, the Department requests more information on how the discharge reached the other side of 16H and how the operator intends to remediate any impacted material below the GPUs. The Department requests information on how the amount spilled was quantified. The Department also requests a copy of the waste manifest once it is available. In reference to the 8/15/2020 spill, it appears that sump has been back filled (Photo 19). The Department requests documentation including photographs of the remediation effort prior to filling in the excavated area and including conductivity readings adjacent to and under the GPU. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the discharge to the ground associated with GPU 3H. Violations associated with the spill that occurred on 8/15/2020 and referenced in IR 3096843 will remain outstanding. Pending the operators response, further violations may be issued.

Comments: On May 11th 2023, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well. The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. There were erosion and sedimentation issues onsite due to the pump jack actively releasing fluid onto the ground. There were observed leaks and discharge on the ground and around the wellhead. The Department observed the pump jack is actively releasing a fluid (where the pump jack enters the wellhead) to the ground. This active release is causing erosion to occur in the adjacent field. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The Department requests the operator provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. Soil conductivity readings were taken at 2 points on the site of the stained soil. The soil conductivity readings were out of range (above 20.00mS). Soil samples were also taken at three points(see photos 9,10,11). Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued. Additional violations maybe forthcoming pending further review of sampling results.

The well cellars are filled in with gravel. There are 5 GPUs and 4 steel vertical production fluids tanks onsite. Both the GPUs and production fluid tanks are stationed in secondary containment. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. The conductivity of the accumulated water in the northwest stormwater vault was 851 uS/cm. The conductivity of the accumulated water in the southwest stormwater vault was 651 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.5 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 20.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 21.6 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 15.4 uS/cm. Stream 1 control site had a conductivity of 20 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 95.2 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 78.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 36.5 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 29.6 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 48.2 uS/cm. Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of at least 5 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and stormwater was discovered on the well pad following a re-frac on the 5H well. The notification also stated that a contractor, Tobias, would excavate the impacted pad material. I met with company man Levi Lee upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release. It rained steadily during this inspection. Tobias had already scraped a thin layer of gravel off of the top of the impacted area at the time of inspection. Mr. Lee said that Creston Environmental was also present to take samples and characterize the release. Some areas of the impacted pad area were more damp than others. No standing fluid was observed in this area of the well pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material according to the Hanna soil conductivity meter ranged from 0.41 mS/cm to 2.86 mS/cm. The higher EC readings were found closer to the well heads and the lower readings were taken farther away from the well heads toward the southeast pad edge. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted.Violations remain outstanding for the release from June 1, 2026. These violations will be closed upon demonstration of Act 2 remediation standards.

Comments: On 6/18/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill (CTS-398645) at the PA Game Commission well pad in Blaine Township, Washington County. The spill reportedly occurred on 6/17/2026 at 8:05 PM, when approximately 20 gallons of produced water/condensate released from a water hauler truck. The Department received the spill report from the operator on the same day at 9:59 PM. The operator reported that the spill was in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 8/06/2018The following was observed during the inspection:The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The reported location of the spill is freshly backfilled with stone, with no residual staining was observed in the remediated area (photo 14). A rolloff box is on site that reportedly contains the impacted material (photo 11). The old GPU/Vertical Separator Units are not equipped with secondary containment (photo 12). However, the associated gas wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The new GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photo 13). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are on site (photos 6 and 7). The ERP appears to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Well 9H is equipped with a well tag (photos 9 and 10). Five additional gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 8). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h). No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas wells.The well pad and access road appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2-5).Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being noted and immediately corrected against the 6/17/2026 produced water/condensate release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Inspection Date: 1/27/2025
Comments: On 12/27/2024 an Incident Response inspection was conducted the MOR42 Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/27/2024 CNX Resources Representative, Ben Geary, reported an approximately 40-gallon brine release off containment at the MOR42 Well Pad located in East Finley Township, Washington County.CNX Resources representative, Ben Geary, and SPSI representative, Mac Maydak, were on site at time of inspection. Mr. Geary informed the Department that that the release was discovered on Saturday, January 25 at 1:15 pm, that the quantity released was approximately 40 gallons, and that a contractor (SPSI) had been dispatched the same day. Mr. Maydak stated that his crew was dispatched on Saturday (1/25) at approximately 1:40 pm. The origin of the release was stated to be a crack found on a T-joint along a line connecting to a slug catcher to the production tanks, which could be observed in front of the Unit H Gas Processing Unit (GPU).Mr. Geary stated that remediation efforts had taken place Saturday (1/25), Sunday (1/26), and continued into today (1/27). The area remediated at the time of inspection measured approximately 38 by 18 feet and to a depth of 1 inch, excluding the sump created on the western side of the GPU that measured approximately 8 inches in depth. It was made known that field screening was conducted during the remediation efforts with screening values between 2,000 and 12,000 s/cm observed. Mr. Maydak stated that 4 Vac boxes had been filled with removed material at the time of inspection.Mr. Geary stated that the remediation efforts would continue until all conductivity values were below 3,000 s/cm and that the sump would be monitored and any fluid that appears would be screened and removed via vac truck.PA DEP Conductivity probe calibrated on 12/27/2024.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1).-A crew was on site remediating near the Unit H GPU. A vac truck and vac box were observed near the remediation site (Photos 2-3).-The remediation area near the Unit H GPU and the source of the release were observed. A crack was observed on the T-joint of a line beneath a lock out-tag out tag. The lines appeared to be coated in a white film, obscuring visual observations (Photos 4-6).-The excavated areas located in front of and on the west side of the GPU were observed. It appeared that pad aggregate had been removed down to the larger riprap (Photos 7-8).-Field soil conductivity screening was conducted in various locations of the remediation site. The bottom and side walls of the sump were screened, with conductivity values ranging between1.682 ms/cm(1,682s/cm) and 4.71 ms/cm observed. Screening was conducted along the northern edge of the GPU and values of 2.56 ms/cm and 1.927 ms/cm (1,682s/cm) were observed. An area in front of the adjacent equipment on the western side of the GPU was screened. Values in this area ranged between 2.66 ms/cm and 11.69 ms/cm (Photos 9 -16).Determination:Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the release. A violation of 78a64a(a) is being issued for the lack of secondary containment.
